sources.verifiedBy: NOT READ FROM THE AGENCY'S DOCUMENT. mass.gov answers every automated request with HTTP 403 ('This page is forbidden'), which was respected and not worked around. The filing frequencies, thresholds and due dates below come from two search-engine summaries (2026-11-05) of https://www.mass.gov/info-details/withholding-tax-guide, https://www.mass.gov/info-details/form-m-941-instructions-tax-return-of-income-taxes-withheld and https://www.mass.gov/regulations/830-CMR-62b21-withholding-of-taxes-on-wages-and-other-payments; the summaries agreed with each other and said the regulation page is about seven years old. Every result built on this profile carries the warning state_source_secondary.

efile.text: MDOR requires submitters to transmit Form W-2 electronically using the MDOR's integrated online tax system. Registered users, employers and third party service agents must upload W-2 reports directly through their MassTaxConnect account.

returns.name: Form M-941, Employer's Return of Income Taxes Withheld
contents: Annual filers: return and payment by January 31; quarterly: by the last day of the month after the quarter; monthly: by the 15th of the following month (March, June, September and December wages by the last day of the following month); employers over $25,000 file quarterly through MassTaxConnect and pay on the quarter-monthly schedule.
A return showing zero tax due must be e-filed through MassTaxConnect; one period per return; payment is due with the return for the annual, quarterly and monthly schedules.
(Dates come from a secondary source; see the profile's first source.)

returns.name: Form M-3, Reconciliation of Massachusetts Income Taxes Withheld for Employers
contents: Filed with Forms W-2, Copy 1, on or before January 31; it reconciles the year's quarterly or monthly M-941 amounts withheld and remitted to the W-2 totals and the number of W-2s enclosed.
This one is read from the Department's own stored form (Rev. 11/16).

deposits.interpretation: SECONDARY SOURCE (see the profile's first source): Massachusetts sets the filing frequency from the employer's PROJECTED annual withholding: $100 or less ANNUAL (Form M-941, return and payment by January 31 of the new year); $101 to $1,200 QUARTERLY (by the last day of the month after the quarter); $1,201 to $25,000 MONTHLY (by the 15th of the following month, except wages of March, June, September and December, due the last day of the following month); MORE than $25,000 (the large-employer, accelerated schedule): quarterly returns through MassTaxConnect by the last day of the month after the quarter, with payments on a deposit schedule: when the Massachusetts tax withheld and not yet paid is $500 or more at the end of a quarter-monthly period (the 7th, 15th, 22nd or last day of the month), it must be paid within 3 business days after that period; whatever is below $500 at quarter end is paid with the quarterly return. A late deposit by a large employer draws a 5% penalty. INTERPRETATION: the $500 test is applied to the amount withheld and not previously paid over, carried forward and restarted each quarter (the regulation, which the summary calls old, words it as the cumulative amount not previously paid over at the end of any quarter-monthly period). The frequency is an INPUT (the Department assigns it from the projected figure) or is derived from a supplied projected annual withholding. A return showing zero must still be e-filed in MassTaxConnect.
